name: Service worker lifetime
plain: A background script registered by a site that persists after the tab is closed.
meaning: It can intercept every request, serve cached content, and wake for push or sync even when no page is open. The browser stops it after about 30 seconds idle, but the registration stays until cleared. Safari deletes it after 7 days of non use.

access.persistence: Registration persists with no fixed expiry. Script checked for update at most every 24 hours. Idle stop after about 30 s (Chrome)
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can keep a background helper script for a site that stays after you close the tab
limits.user_action: Nothing. It is set up the first time you visit a site that uses one
can: Intercept the site's own requests and serve saved copies
Wake for push or sync when you allow them
Keep the helper registered until you clear it or the site removes it
Make a site load fast and work offline
cannot: See other sites' requests or data, since it is limited to the one site
Stay running, as the browser stops it after about 30 seconds idle
Last in Safari beyond 7 days without a visit
Survive when you clear that site's data
limits.differs: Safari deletes a site's helper after 7 days without use. Chrome, Edge and Firefox keep it until cleared.

story.what_it_is: A background script a site installs, which stays on your device after you close the tab.

marketing.name: Tracking prevention
marketing.pitch: Safari limits how long background scripts and site data can live for sites you do not use.

story.for_you: You never see it. A site you visited can leave a small helper that makes it load faster and work offline. It can also stay around for a long time unless the browser clears it.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for offline, caching, push and fast loads. It acts like a tiny server on your device. It can also keep an identity link or run tracking code, so browsers limit its lifetime.

use_cases.example: A news site caches pages so you can read offline on a plane.
A browser game caches its files, so it starts in a second the next time and works offline.
A web editor like Google Docs keeps its code locally so it opens fast and works offline.
A store caches its catalog so browsing feels instant on a weak signal.
An ad or tracking script installs a helper to survive cookie clearing and measure visits later.
A web chat uses a helper to receive push messages when the tab is closed.
A malicious site installs a helper that keeps showing spam alerts after you leave.

technical_bounds: Idle termination about 30 s, single event up to about 5 min (Chrome)
Safari 7 day cap on registrations without user visit

abuse: Persistent hidden request interception, tracker caching

history.change: ITP 7 day storage cap covers registrations
